<reason>Side A won by keeping the motion as written at the center: fines hit the named public-facing service on a basic-standards checklist, including when the operator cannot rewrite a locked vendor stack. Side B’s admission that it would still fine that hospital made “repeatedly” look like a surcharge on incapacity rather than proof of refusal, and the “both” answer on checklist vs. task completion never restored a clean trigger. Side B’s live residual—who forces procurement if not an external cost—was real but overclaimed that only post-hoc fines have teeth, while a clipped opening and a late metric wobble capped the case.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s pressure on whether a second failed audit of an unrewritable third-party scheduler is a “decision,” then using B’s “yes, still fine them” answer to recast the resolution as billing incapacity rather than deterring refusal.</best_rebuttal>
